uncertainObservations: Both moons are crescents lit on the lower-right limb with the unlit remainder faintly visible; the smaller one is dim enough that I checked it twice, but I am confident there really are TWO separate moons in this sky.
The small upright object on the table between the letter and the armillary sphere may be a miniature sword stood point-down, a cross, or a candlestick; I cannot tell.
I cannot read any of the writing on the held letter.
The central sword's blade is partly lost in the glare where it enters the heart, so I cannot confirm whether its point emerges below.
I found no clearly drawn cast shadow anywhere in this card, so I report no shadow direction.
The number of orbit circles and stars is uncountable and I did not attempt it.

uncertainObservations: This is the darkest of the eight. I brightened it more than three times over and large parts of the frame still hold no recoverable detail; several readings here are low-confidence.
The number of carried swords cannot be determined: three grips plus one cross-guard are resolvable, a fourth may be hidden, and the blade count below the hand reads as three or four.
No face is visible at all, so I cannot say whether he is looking ahead, down or back — I can only say the head is not turned back toward the viewer.
Whether the two structures are stone cairns/tombs, shingled huts or stiffened tents is ambiguous; they have doorways and roof finials.
The source of the upper-left glow is not drawn; it could be a moon behind cloud, a lamp out of frame or a lit opening.
I cannot confirm whether the planted swords' points are driven into the earth or merely hidden behind foreground stones.
